sentences.text: The parties will be referred to, as per their status before the Tribunal, for the sake of convenience.

3. The brief facts of the case are, the son of petitioner Nos.1 and 2 and brother of the petitioner No.3 namely Sri.G.G.Sridhara, the deceased, met with an accident on 25.04.2013 while traveling as loader in the tractor and trailer bearing No.KA517923-7924 at Honnashettihalli Road, Alfaz Nagar,
Channarayapatna and later died in the District Hospital.

The petitioners being the dependents,
approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the owner and insurer of the vehicle.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence, by the impugned judgment, awarded compensation of Rs.6,05,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% p.m., from the date of petitioner till realization from respondent No.1 - owner of the vehicle.
4. Being aggrieved by the same, the owner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

Heard the arguments of Sri.Halesha R.G., learned counsel for the appellant/respondent No.1/owner and Sri. O.Mahesh, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Sri.M.N. Ningaraj,
learned counsel for the petitioners.

6. It is the contention of learned counsel for the owner of the tractor and trailer that the tractor is covered by package policy that the deceased was allowed by the driver of the tractor to travel and he was succumbed to death in the accident.

The risk of the deceased is covered under the package policy and the Tribunal is committed an error in fastening the liability and sought for direction to the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured.

7. Per contra, Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that Ex.R2 is the policy issued, a specific note that there is no coverage to the employee, paid driver or cleaner.
The package policy is different and it will not cover the risk of the passengers carried in the tractor.
No premium is paid for the NC: 2023:KHC:41021 passenger of the tractor.
The package policy covers the risk of the third parties and also the agricultural produce transported in the tractor.
The Tribunal has taken consideration of these aspects and fastened the liability against the owner of the vehicle and he supported the impugned judgment.
8. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that irrespective of the liability either of the owner or the insurer, they may be directed to deposit the compensation, as early as possible.
9. I gave my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the materials on record.
10. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident and death of the deceased in the accident, the petitioners being the parents and brother, entitled to grant of compensation.
Since the petitioners have not filed any appeal, there is no question of going to assessment of quantum of compensation.
The only issue is, liability on NC: 2023:KHC:41021 the part of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured.
11. Admittedly, the tractor and trailer is covered with an insurance and the policy of the insurance is available as per Ex.R2.
The driver of the tractor owning valid driving license on the date of accident.

The policy of insurance is defined as package policy and there is a specific endorsement in the schedule of premium that premium paid to the employee of the insured, paid drivers, cleaners, etc.,
premium paid is zero.
The tractor is covered with the own damage coverage and also basic third party liability.
But, the deceased was a third party as claimed by the owner of the tractor, is to be examined.
The tractor having a seating capacity of one for the driver, there is no provision for carrying any passengers including the labourers in the tractor or trailer.
At the time of accident, the deceased was the passenger.

12. Having regard to the premium schedule, the zero premium is paid for the employee, paid drivers and NC: 2023:KHC:41021 cleaners, the risk of the third party alone comes to as a passenger of the Umesh vs The Manager on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98128143/
3 tractor but passenger is not a third party.
Therefore, the policy under Ex.R2 does not cover the risk of the deceased.
The Tribunal has considered this aspect and fastened the liability against the owner to pay the compensation.
I do not find any error or irregularities committed by the Tribunal.

Hence,
the appeal devoid of merits.

In the result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is dismissed.
ii) The amount in deposit shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
